items.title: Why does message size make the split-message bug more likely?
items.description: This is an illustrative model, not a precise network simulation — real fragmentation depends on the OS, network path, and buffering, not just size. But it captures the real shape of the problem: a message much smaller than a typical network buffer usually arrives in one piece, while a message spanning several buffers' worth of data is far more likely to be split across multiple 'data' events, exactly the condition the chat server's bug depended on.
items.compute: const typicalBufferBytes = 1460; const minimumFragments = Math.ceil(params.messageSizeBytes / typicalBufferBytes); return { minimumFragments };

outputs.label: Minimum possible fragments this message could split across
